title: Forged status line via newline injection in displayed text
root_cause: Attacker-controlled text is rendered inside a trusted interface with no escaping, so the attacker can shape what the user believes the program said. The code ran correctly; the user was deceived. The same idea underlies clickjacking, spoofed dialogs, and terminal escape-sequence injection.
defenses: Escape or strip control characters (newlines, ESC sequences, bidi overrides) before showing untrusted text.
Show security-relevant status (verified / unverified) from the real check, in a visually separate, unforgeable area.
Quote or visually frame untrusted values so they cannot read as part of the interface itself.
Default to the unsafe-looking state: when verification is absent or fails, say so prominently.
For web UIs, use frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options and confirm dangerous actions out-of-band.
